applied_adjustments.name: business_hours_known_entity
applied_adjustments.reason: Most legitimate card-present and online shopping happens in local working hours; a card group we have seen before transacting at that time is the least surprising case. Local hour is an estimate (K-06, offset -6 h) and weekday uses the reference calendar (assumption 4).

applied_adjustments.name: foreign_country
applied_adjustments.reason: Cross-border transactions are a classic risk factor (card used outside its home market). addr2 = 87 = US is a community interpretation (assumption 3).

applied_adjustments.name: product_c
applied_adjustments.reason: Business logic: C is a minority product (11.6% of rows) that mostly (91%) comes with online identity/device data and mostly (95%) without a billing country, i.e. a card-not-present, likely cross-border digital channel where goods are delivered instantly and resale is easy. Small base factor. The EDA fit table (docs/eda.md) was used only as a plausibility check, not to choose the value.

applied_adjustments.name: low_volume_high_amount
applied_adjustments.reason: Large purchases in the hours when few customers are active are a common account-takeover pattern (fraudster acts while the owner sleeps). Only high amounts are boosted so that ordinary night activity is not penalized.

applied_adjustments.name: new_card_high_amount
applied_adjustments.reason: A large purchase on the first day of a card is a known bust-out / stolen-card pattern; a genuine new customer usually starts small. D1 = card age is a data-supported assumption (5).

applied_adjustments.name: product_w
applied_adjustments.reason: Business logic: W is the mainstream product (74.5% of rows); the anomaly layers' notion of normal is calibrated mostly on it, so small tolerance. EDA used only as a plausibility check.
